Tibetan Spaniel Health Net

Discover a compassionate community dedicated to fostering health support and well-being for Tibetan Spaniels. Join us in our mission to provide resources, education, and collaboration to enhance the overall health and well-being of Tibetan Spaniels and their owners.

About Tibetan Spaniel Health Net

1/10

Our Beginning

In 1990 Deb Henson started the Tibetan Spaniel Pedigree Database. Jan Allinder created the Tibetan Spaniel Network website in 1996. Recognizing the importance of having a resource for breeders to make informed decisions, the Pedigree Database was incorporated into the Tibetan Spaniel Network in 2000.

 

In 2023, Diana Gerba lost her boy Marco and vowed that part of his legacy would be to further evolve the database to include more health data. To ensure their joint endeavor continues into the future a group of dedicated Tibbie lovers joined together and have formed the Tibetan Spaniel Health Net Inc., a 501(c)(3) charitable organization dedicated to maintaining an international health and pedigree database through voluntary submission

Meet The Board

Our Mission

Our Commitment

The Tibetan Spaniel Health Net is dedicated to advancing the health of Tibetan Spaniels by educating the general public, breeders and scientists, fostering collaboration, and providing resources to reduce genetic disease.

Our Vision

That all Tibetan Spaniels live long and healthy lives.

Our Objectives

Support health research into genetic diseases through:

Worldwide Team

Forming a worldwide team of data operators to check and verify much of the information before it is allowed to be visible in the database,

Collaborating

Collaborating with the scientific community to support health research relevant to the Tibetan Spaniels.

Maintaining a database

Sharing data

Maintaining an international health and pedigree database through voluntary submissions from owners, breeders, and other sources.

Open-sharing of data and information with the general public, Tibetan Spaniel owners, breeders, and scientists.
